# brig sandbox snapshot

Keep copies of a sandbox's /sandbox in its VM, and bring them back

## Synopsis

```text
brig sandbox snapshot COMMAND
```

## Description

A snapshot is a copy of one sandbox's /sandbox, with a record of the
sandbox: its image, providers, policy and services. It lives in the VM, on the
data disk next to the sandboxes, and outlives the sandbox it came from. It is
named SANDBOX@TIME, the time in UTC, and belongs to the sandbox's workspace.

The data disk is btrfs, so a snapshot shares its blocks with the sandbox it
came from: it takes seconds and almost no space when it is taken, and grows
only as the sandbox moves on. [`brig sandbox snapshot list`](brig-sandbox-snapshot-list.md) shows what each one
holds alone, which is what deleting it frees.

Snapshots go with the VM: [`brig delete`](brig-delete.md) removes them with it. Push code to git
as before.

The [global options](brig.md#options) of brig apply too.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`brig sandbox snapshot create`](brig-sandbox-snapshot-create.md) | Take a snapshot of a sandbox's /sandbox |
| [`brig sandbox snapshot delete`](brig-sandbox-snapshot-delete.md) | Delete snapshots |
| [`brig sandbox snapshot list`](brig-sandbox-snapshot-list.md) | List the snapshots in a VM, with the space they take |
| [`brig sandbox snapshot prune`](brig-sandbox-snapshot-prune.md) | Delete the snapshots of deleted sandboxes and old snapshots |
| [`brig sandbox snapshot restore`](brig-sandbox-snapshot-restore.md) | Replace a sandbox's /sandbox with a snapshot |
